title: PM-KISAN
objective: Yearly income support for landholding farmer families.
eligibility: Farmer families that hold cultivable land in their names, unless they fall under the scheme's exclusion categories (for example certain higher-income groups). Check the exclusion list in the official FAQ.
benefits: Rs 6,000 per year per family, paid in three instalments of Rs 2,000 every four months, directly into the bank account.
how_to_apply: Register on pmkisan.gov.in using 'New Farmer Registration', or go to a Common Service Centre, or approach the village revenue official (patwari). e-KYC is mandatory to keep receiving payments.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Bank account linked to Aadhaar; Land ownership records; Mobile number
summary_en: If your family owns farmland, this scheme sends Rs 6,000 a year straight to your bank account in three parts. You must register, complete e-KYC, and your family must not fall in an excluded group. Check your status on the official site before relying on a payment.
summary_hi: अगर आपके परिवार के पास खेती योग्य ज़मीन है, तो यह योजना आपके बैंक खाते में प्रति वर्ष ₹6,000 तीन समान किश्तों में सीधे भेजती है। योजना का लाभ निरंतर प्राप्त करने के लिए e-KYC पूरा करना अनिवार्य है।

title: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
department: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (National Health Authority)
objective: Free hospital treatment cover for eligible poor families and for all citizens aged 70 and above.
eligibility: Families identified under the scheme's criteria (based on the SECC 2011 data), and every citizen aged 70 or above regardless of income through the Ayushman Vay Vandana card.
benefits: Cashless cover of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year for hospital treatment at empanelled hospitals. Seniors aged 70+ in families already covered get an extra top-up of up to Rs 5 lakh for themselves.
how_to_apply: Check eligibility on the official PM-JAY site or the Ayushman app, then get your card through the app or portal, a Common Service Centre, or an empanelled hospital. Seniors aged 70+ can self-register for the Vay Vandana card.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Mobile number
summary_en: This scheme pays for hospital treatment up to Rs 5 lakh a year per family at listed hospitals, without you paying upfront. Poor families that meet the official criteria are covered, and anyone aged 70 or above can get a card whatever their income. Treatment must be at an empanelled hospital.
summary_hi: यह योजना सूचीबद्ध अस्पतालों में पात्र गरीब परिवारों तथा 70 वर्ष या उससे अधिक आयु के सभी वरिष्ठ नागरिकों को प्रति वर्ष ₹5 लाख तक का कैशलेस इलाज प्रदान करती है।

title: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana
objective: Clean cooking gas connections for women in poor households.
eligibility: An adult woman (18 years or older) from an eligible poor household that does not already have an LPG connection.
benefits: A deposit-free LPG connection in the woman's name. Under Ujjwala 2.0, the first refill and a stove are also free.
how_to_apply: Apply through pmuy.gov.in or give the filled KYC form and documents to a nearby LPG distributor. The connection is released after verification.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Ration card or equivalent household proof; Bank account details; Filled KYC application form
summary_en: This scheme gives eligible women a gas connection without a security deposit, plus a free stove and first cylinder refill under Ujjwala 2.0. Later refills are paid by the family. Only households with no existing LPG connection can apply.
summary_hi: यह योजना पात्र गरीब परिवारों की वयस्क महिलाओं को बिना सुरक्षा जमा के मुफ्त एलपीजी गैस कनेक्शन, पहला भरा सिलेंडर और चूल्हा प्रदान करती है।

title: National Education Policy 2020
objective: National framework to reform school and higher education.
eligibility: Not an application-based scheme. It is a policy that applies to schools, colleges and universities, and is carried out by the Centre and state governments.
benefits: Replaces the old 10+2 school structure with a 5+3+3+4 structure (ages 3-8, 8-11, 11-14, 14-18), stresses basic reading and maths in early years, flexible multidisciplinary choices, and use of the home language or mother tongue in the early years.
how_to_apply: No application is needed. Changes reach students through their schools, boards and universities. Follow the Ministry of Education for official documents and updates.
summary_en: NEP 2020 is the Government of India's plan for how school and college education should work. It was approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 July 2020. Its main change is a new school structure covering ages 3 to 18, with more focus on early learning and flexible subject choices. Each state decides the pace of its own rollout.
summary_hi: राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति 2020 भारतीय शिक्षा प्रणाली में 5+3+3+4 संरचना लागू करती है, जिसमें प्रारंभिक वर्षों में मातृभाषा में शिक्षा और कौशल विकास पर विशेष ध्यान दिया गया है।

title: Atal Pension Yojana
objective: Guaranteed monthly pension after age 60, mainly for unorganised-sector workers.
eligibility: Indian citizens aged 18 to 40 with a savings bank or post office account. From 1 October 2022, anyone who is or has been an income-tax payer cannot join.
benefits: A guaranteed pension of Rs 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 or 5,000 per month from age 60, as chosen at joining. The same pension continues to the spouse. Monthly contribution depends on the age at joining and the pension chosen.
how_to_apply: Go to your bank or post office branch (or use net banking or the bank's app) and fill the APY form. Contributions are auto-debited from your savings account each month.
documents_required: Savings bank or post office account; ID proof (Aadhaar is commonly used); Mobile number
summary_en: You pay a small amount every month while working, and from age 60 you receive a fixed monthly pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000, depending on the plan you choose. The earlier you join, the less you pay each month. Income-tax payers cannot join.
summary_hi: असंगठित क्षेत्र के कामगारों के लिए एक निश्चित पेंशन योजना, जिसमें 18 से 40 वर्ष की आयु में जुड़ने पर 60 वर्ष की आयु से ₹1,000 से ₹5,000 की गारंटीशुदा मासिक पेंशन मिलती है।

title: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana
objective: Loans for small non-farm businesses.
eligibility: Individuals and small businesses in manufacturing, trading or services that need a loan of up to Rs 20 lakh. Tarun Plus is only for borrowers who have fully repaid an earlier Tarun loan.
benefits: Loans in four bands: Shishu up to Rs 50,000, Kishore above Rs 50,000 up to Rs 5 lakh, Tarun above Rs 5 lakh up to Rs 10 lakh, and Tarun Plus above Rs 10 lakh up to Rs 20 lakh. Interest rates and fees are set by each lender.
how_to_apply: Apply at a bank, NBFC or microfinance institution, or through the Udyamimitra portal linked from mudra.org.in. Choose the band that matches your funding need.
documents_required: Identity proof; Address proof; Business proof or simple business plan; Bank statements (usually asked for larger loans)
summary_en: Mudra loans help small shops, workshops and service businesses get money to start or grow. The size of the loan decides the category, from Shishu (small) up to Tarun Plus. You apply to a bank or lender, which decides approval and interest.
summary_hi: गैर-कॉर्पोरेट और गैर-कृषि लघु उद्यमियों व छोटे व्यवसायों के लिए बैंकों और वित्तीय संस्थानों के माध्यम से ₹20 लाख तक का आसान ऋण उपलब्ध कराने की योजना।

title: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0
objective: Help urban families buy, build or rent a pucca home.
eligibility: Urban families in the EWS (income up to Rs 3 lakh), LIG (Rs 3-6 lakh) or MIG (Rs 6-9 lakh) groups per year, with no pucca house anywhere in India in the family's name. A beneficiary can use only one vertical.
benefits: Central assistance of up to Rs 2.50 lakh per unit, and an interest subsidy on eligible home loans sanctioned on or after 1 September 2024. Verticals include building on your own land, affordable housing in partnership, affordable rental housing and the interest subsidy scheme.
how_to_apply: Apply on the official PMAY-U 2.0 portal after reading the instructions for your vertical. Keep Aadhaar and income details ready.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Income details or proof; Bank account details
summary_en: This scheme helps city families without a pucca house to build, buy or rent one. How much help you get depends on your yearly household income group and the vertical you choose. Rural families should look at PMAY-Gramin instead, which is a separate scheme.
summary_hi: शहरी गरीब और मध्यम वर्गीय परिवारों (EWS, LIG, MIG) को पक्का घर खरीदने, निर्माण करने या किफायती किराए पर लेने के लिए वित्तीय सहायता और ब्याज सब्सिडी देती है।

title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023
objective: Law protecting people's digital personal data.
eligibility: Applies to every person whose digital personal data is handled by an organisation. No application is needed.
benefits: You can ask an organisation for information about your data, ask for corrections and deletion, nominate someone to act for you, and complain to the Data Protection Board. Organisations must respond to requests within a maximum of 90 days.
how_to_apply: First contact the organisation that holds your data using its grievance process. If you are not satisfied, complain to the Data Protection Board. Check the MeitY site for the current process.
summary_en: This law gives you rights over the digital data that companies and government bodies collect about you, and sets duties for them. Parliament passed the Act in August 2023 and the Rules were notified in November 2025, with some parts taking effect in stages. It is a law, not a benefit scheme.
summary_hi: डिजिटल व्यक्तिगत डेटा की सुरक्षा और गोपनीयता सुनिश्चित करने वाला कानून, जो नागरिकों को अपने व्यक्तिगत डेटा पर अधिकार और कंपनियों पर जवाबदेही तय करता है।

title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
objective: Crop insurance that protects farmers against losses from natural calamities, pests and diseases.
eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers, whether loanee or non-loanee.
benefits: Comprehensive insurance coverage against non-preventable natural risks (drought, flood, pests, post-harvest losses). Farmers pay low actuarial premium (2% for Kharif, 1.5% for Rabi, 5% for commercial/horticultural crops) with government subsidizing the rest.
how_to_apply: Apply through the official PMFBY portal (pmfby.gov.in), nearest Common Service Centre (CSC), or directly through your bank branch / primary agricultural credit society within the cutoff date.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Bank passbook/account details; Land record (RoR/Khasra/Khatauni); Sowing certificate or crop declaration; Tenancy agreement (for tenant farmers)
summary_en: A crop insurance scheme run by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. It is meant to protect farmers from financial loss when crops fail because of natural calamities, pests or disease. Farmers usually enrol through their bank, a Common Service Centre or the official crop insurance portal.

title: Kisan Credit Card Scheme
objective: Short-term credit for farmers to meet cultivation and related needs.
eligibility: Individual/joint farmers, owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees, sharecroppers, and SHGs or Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) engaged in agriculture or allied sectors (dairy, poultry, fisheries).
benefits: Timely short-term credit with flexible revolving cash credit facility. Concessional interest rate of 7% p.a., effectively 4% p.a. with prompt repayment incentive (3% subvention) up to Rs 3 lakh (Rs 2 lakh for allied activities).
how_to_apply: Submit the simplified common KCC application form to any commercial bank, regional rural bank (RRB), or cooperative bank branch, or apply via the official banking portal.
documents_required: Aadhaar; PAN card or Form 60; Land ownership documents or tenancy certificate; Crop pattern details; Passport size photograph
summary_en: A credit scheme that lets farmers borrow money from banks for cultivation and related needs. The card works like a credit limit that farmers can use again and again, and it can also cover allied activities such as dairy and fisheries. Farmers apply at their bank branch.

title: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana
objective: Better irrigation coverage and more efficient water use on farms.
eligibility: Farmers and farmer groups, SHGs, cooperatives, and water user associations owning or cultivating agricultural land with access to water sources.
benefits: Subsidies (up to 45-55% depending on farm size and category) for installation of micro-irrigation systems (drip and sprinkler), farm ponds, water harvesting structures, and assured end-to-end irrigation infrastructure.
how_to_apply: Register online via your respective state agriculture or horticulture department portal, or submit an application through the district horticulture/agriculture office.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Land revenue records (7/12 extract or Khatauni); Bank passbook; Electricity connection details (for electric pump sets); Category certificate (if applicable)
summary_en: A national scheme to bring water to more farms and use it better. It supports irrigation projects and water-saving methods such as drip and sprinkler systems, with the aim of getting more crop for every drop of water.

title: Soil Health Card Scheme
objective: Soil testing and cards that guide farmers on the right nutrients and fertiliser use.
eligibility: All landholding farmers across India. Soil samples are collected periodically across village grids.
benefits: Free cycle-based Soil Health Card indicating status of 12 critical nutrients (macro, secondary, and micronutrients) along with customized fertiliser and soil amendment dosage recommendations to cut costs and maximize yield.
how_to_apply: No direct application required. State agriculture department officials or village coordinators collect soil samples. Farmers can track sample status and download cards from soilhealth.dac.gov.in.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Land record / Khasra number; Mobile number
summary_en: Under this scheme, farmers receive a soil health card that reports the nutrient status of their land and suggests which fertilisers and how much suit their soil. The aim is to cut unnecessary fertiliser use and improve yields. Soil samples are collected and tested through government laboratories.

title: e-NAM National Agriculture Market
objective: Online trading platform that links agricultural markets across the country.
eligibility: Farmers, registered traders, commission agents, and Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) operating in mandis integrated with the e-NAM platform.
benefits: Access to a nationwide electronic trading portal linking APMC mandis, transparent real-time bidding, wider buyer competition, digital quality assaying, and direct online bank payments without middlemen.
how_to_apply: Register on the official e-NAM portal (enam.gov.in) or mobile app, or register at the e-NAM help desk at your local participating APMC mandi.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Bank passbook/account details; Mandi trade license or farmer registration ID; Mobile number
summary_en: e-NAM is an online trading platform that connects agricultural produce markets (mandis) across states. Farmers and traders can see prices and trade through one platform, which is meant to give farmers a wider choice of buyers and more transparent prices.

title: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana
objective: Pension scheme for small and marginal farmers.
eligibility: Small and marginal farmers (SMFs) aged between 18 and 40 years holding cultivable land up to 2 hectares, not covered under NPS, ESIC, EPFO or paying income tax.
benefits: Assured monthly pension of Rs 3,000 upon reaching age 60. Monthly contribution ranges from Rs 55 to Rs 200 based on entry age, matched equally by the Central Government. 50% family pension for surviving spouse.
how_to_apply: Visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with documents or self-enroll on the official Maandhan portal (maandhan.in). Contributions can be auto-debited from PM-KISAN bank accounts.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Savings bank account details / Jan Dhan account; Land ownership documents (Khasra/Khatauni); Mobile number
summary_en: A voluntary pension scheme for small and marginal farmers. Farmers who join pay a small monthly contribution and, after a certain age, receive a regular pension. Check the official site for the age limits, contribution and pension amounts.

title: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana
objective: Support for farmers who adopt organic farming in clusters.
eligibility: Farmers willing to adopt certified organic farming practices by forming clusters of 20 or more farmers covering a minimum of 20 hectares (or 50 acres).
benefits: Financial assistance of Rs 50,000 per hectare over 3 years, of which Rs 31,000 is directly provided for organic inputs (bio-fertilizers, vermicompost, botanical extracts), certification, and marketing.
how_to_apply: Form a cluster and register with the District Agriculture Office, Regional Council, or through the PGS-India portal (pgsindia-ncof.gov.in).
documents_required: Aadhaar; Bank account details; Land ownership records; Group resolution and cluster member roster
summary_en: This scheme encourages farmers to move to organic farming by forming groups (clusters) that follow organic methods together. It supports training, inputs and certification, so that farmers can get a better market for organic produce.

title: Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana
objective: Funds to states for agriculture and allied sector development.
eligibility: State agriculture departments, agricultural universities, FPOs, and farmer cooperatives implementing public agricultural development projects.
benefits: Decentralized central funding assistance to states for agricultural infrastructure, value addition, agri-business incubation, seed production, and innovation projects.
how_to_apply: Agri-entrepreneurs and FPOs can submit project proposals under designated RKVY-RAFTAAR incubation centers or state agriculture departments.
documents_required: Project proposal; Organization/FPO registration documents; Bank details; Land or facility proof
summary_en: A scheme through which the Centre gives funds to states for agriculture and related sectors. States use the money for projects they choose, such as farm infrastructure, better seeds and farm machinery, so it works mostly through state agriculture departments rather than direct applications.

title: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM)
objective: Solar pumps and solar power for farmers to cut diesel use and earn extra income.
eligibility: Individual farmers, groups of farmers, cooperatives, panchayats, and FPOs with agricultural land and need for irrigation pumps.
benefits: Up to 60% capital subsidy (30% Centre + 30% State) for setting up standalone off-grid solar pumps or solarizing existing grid-connected agricultural pumps, plus option to sell surplus power to the grid.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the respective State Renewable Energy Development Agency (SREDA) portal or state agriculture portal linked from pmkusum.mnre.gov.in.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Land ownership records; Bank account passbook; Electricity connection consumer number (for grid-connected pumps)
summary_en: PM-KUSUM promotes solar energy for farmers. It supports solar-powered irrigation pumps and small solar plants on farmland, so farmers can reduce diesel and electricity costs and may earn extra income by selling surplus power. It runs through state agencies.

title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund
objective: Loans with interest support for farm-gate and post-harvest infrastructure.
eligibility: Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Marketing Cooperative Societies, FPOs, SHGs, Joint Liability Groups, agri-entrepreneurs, and startups.
benefits: Medium-to-long term debt financing facility for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets. Provides 3% per annum interest subvention on loans up to Rs 2 crore for up to 7 years, along with CGTMSE credit guarantee.
how_to_apply: Register and submit a Detailed Project Report (DPR) online at the AIF portal (agriinfra.dac.gov.in). Once approved, banks sanction the loan.
documents_required: Entity registration; PAN; Aadhaar of promoters; Detailed Project Report (DPR); Financial statements/ITR; Land documents
summary_en: A financing facility that supports building farm-gate and post-harvest infrastructure such as cold storage, warehouses and processing units. Farmers, farmer groups, agri-entrepreneurs and others can get loans with interest support through banks.

title: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana
department: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
objective: Support for the fisheries sector and for fishers' livelihoods.
eligibility: Fishers, fish farmers, fish workers, SHGs, JLGs, fisheries cooperatives, and fisheries entrepreneurs across marine, inland, and aquaculture sectors.
benefits: Financial assistance covering 40% of project cost for General category and up to 60% for SC/ST/Women for fish ponds, biofloc, RAS systems, cold storage, insulated vehicles, and deep-sea fishing vessels.
how_to_apply: Submit project proposal and application online via pmmsy.dof.gov.in or directly through the District Fisheries Development Officer.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Bank passbook; Land/waterbody ownership or lease deed; Detailed Project Report (DPR); Caste certificate (if seeking SC/ST subsidy)
summary_en: A scheme to develop India's fisheries sector and improve the incomes of people who depend on it. It supports fishing, fish farming, boats, cold chains and related infrastructure, and runs through state fisheries departments.

title: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
objective: Credit-linked support for small food processing businesses to upgrade and formalise.
eligibility: Individual micro food processing units, FPOs, SHGs, and producer cooperatives operating or starting food processing enterprises, based on One District One Product (ODOP) focus.
benefits: Credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% of eligible project cost with a ceiling of Rs 10 lakh per unit. Seed capital of Rs 40,000 per SHG member for working capital and small tools.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the official PMFME portal (pmfme.mofpi.gov.in) with the assistance of district resource persons (DRPs).
documents_required: Aadhaar; PAN; Udyam registration; Bank account statement (past 6 months); Quotations for machinery; Proof of business premises
summary_en: A scheme that helps small food processing businesses upgrade, formalise and grow. It offers credit-linked support and aims to help micro units get access to credit, branding and markets. Applications are handled through state nodal agencies.

title: National Health Mission
objective: Strengthens public health services in rural and urban areas.
eligibility: All citizens across India, with special priority for rural and urban poor, vulnerable communities, pregnant women, and children accessing public healthcare.
benefits: Free essential medicines, free diagnostic services, free maternal and newborn care, and institutional healthcare across Primary Health Centres (PHCs) and Community Health Centres (CHCs).
how_to_apply: No prior enrollment required. Visit any government dispensary, Primary Health Centre, Sub-Centre/Health & Wellness Centre, or government hospital.
documents_required: None mandatory for basic clinical consultation; Identity card (Aadhaar/Voter ID) helpful for records
summary_en: The National Health Mission helps states strengthen public health services in rural and urban areas. It supports health centres, community health workers such as ASHAs, free medicines and maternal and child health programmes. Citizens use these services through their local government health facilities.

title: Janani Suraksha Yojana
objective: Cash support to encourage safe childbirth in health facilities.
eligibility: Pregnant women delivering in government health facilities or accredited private hospitals, with focus on BPL/SC/ST mothers in Low Performing States (LPS).
benefits: Direct cash assistance: Rs 1,400 in rural LPS areas (Rs 1,000 in urban LPS areas) and Rs 700 in rural HPS areas (Rs 600 in urban HPS areas) for institutional delivery.
how_to_apply: Register your pregnancy at the local Anganwadi centre or Primary Health Centre with the local ASHA worker to obtain a Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card.
documents_required: Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card; Aadhaar; Bank account passbook; BPL ration card (for High Performing States)
summary_en: A programme that encourages pregnant women to give birth in hospitals or health centres instead of at home. Eligible women receive cash support, and ASHA workers help women reach the facility. Details differ for rural and urban areas and by state.

title: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana
objective: Cash incentive for pregnant and nursing mothers.
eligibility: Pregnant women and lactating mothers aged 19 or older for the first live birth, and for the second live birth if the child is a girl (excluding regular government/PSU employees).
benefits: Cash incentive of Rs 5,000 in two installments for the first child, and Rs 6,000 in a single installment for the second girl child, transferred via DBT to promote maternal nutrition.
how_to_apply: Apply through the PMMVY portal (pmmvy.wcd.gov.in) or register through the local Anganwadi worker or ASHA within 270 days of the last menstrual period (LMP).
documents_required: Aadhaar of mother and husband; MCP card; Bank passbook linked to Aadhaar; Child birth certificate (for later installment)
summary_en: A maternity benefit scheme that gives pregnant and nursing mothers a cash incentive to help them rest and eat better around childbirth. Payment is made in instalments directly to the bank account. Check the official site for who qualifies.

title: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan
objective: Free antenatal check-ups for pregnant women on the 9th of every month.
eligibility: All pregnant women in their 2nd and 3rd trimesters (after 12 weeks of pregnancy).
benefits: Free, assured, comprehensive antenatal check-ups and diagnostic tests conducted on the 9th day of every month by specialist OB/GYN doctors at designated government health facilities.
how_to_apply: Visit any designated government hospital, CHC, or PHC on the 9th of any month for free check-up and screening.
documents_required: MCP card; Government photo identity card (Aadhaar/Voter ID)
summary_en: Under this programme, pregnant women can get a free check-up from a doctor at government health facilities on the 9th of every month. The goal is to find high-risk pregnancies early and reduce deaths of mothers and babies.

title: Mission Indradhanush
objective: Immunisation drive to cover children and pregnant women who missed vaccines.
eligibility: All partially vaccinated or unvaccinated children under 5 years of age and unvaccinated pregnant women across selected high-focus districts.
benefits: Free immunization against 12 life-threatening vaccine-preventable diseases (diphtheria, whooping cough, tetanus, polio, measles, rubella, childhood TB, hepatitis B, meningitis, pneumonia, rotavirus, and Japanese encephalitis).
how_to_apply: Participate in routine or special intensive vaccination drives at local Anganwadi centres, PHCs, or community vaccination booths organized by ASHAs and ANMs.
documents_required: Child immunization card / MCP card (if available; no child is turned away for lack of documents)
summary_en: A vaccination drive to reach children and pregnant women who missed routine immunisation. Health workers carry out special rounds to give vaccines against preventable diseases. Vaccines are free at government health centres.

title: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission
objective: Digital health IDs and linked health records for citizens.
eligibility: Every citizen of India, healthcare professionals, clinics, labs, and hospitals wishing to participate in the digital health ecosystem.
benefits: Creation of a unique 14-digit Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) number and card, enabling citizens to digitally store, access, and share verifiable medical records across doctors and hospitals nationwide.
how_to_apply: Create your ABHA ID online in under two minutes at abdm.gov.in or using the ABHA / Aarogya Setu app using Aadhaar OTP or driving license.
documents_required: Aadhaar number and linked mobile number (or Driving License)
summary_en: The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission creates a digital health ID for citizens and links health records, doctors and facilities online. With your consent, your records can be shared with a doctor or hospital. Creating an ID is voluntary.

title: Pradhan Mantri Bharatiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
objective: Quality generic medicines at lower prices through Jan Aushadhi Kendras.
eligibility: Open to all citizens seeking affordable generic medicines. Operating licenses are open to pharmacists, NGOs, doctors, and entrepreneurs.
benefits: Quality generic medicines, surgical supplies, and nutraceuticals sold through Jan Aushadhi Kendras at prices 50% to 90% cheaper than branded market alternatives.
how_to_apply: Walk into any of the 10,000+ PM Jan Aushadhi Kendras nationwide with a doctor's prescription. Entrepreneurs can apply to open a Kendra at janaushadhi.gov.in.
documents_required: Doctor's medical prescription (for prescription drugs); None required for over-the-counter wellness products
summary_en: This scheme sets up Jan Aushadhi Kendras that sell quality generic medicines at much lower prices than branded medicines. The Kendras are listed on the official site.

title: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram
objective: Health screening and early treatment for children from birth to 18 years.
eligibility: All children aged 0 to 18 years enrolled in government/aided schools and Anganwadi centres, as well as newborns delivered at public health facilities.
benefits: Free routine screening and early intervention for 4 'D's: Defects at birth, Deficiencies, Diseases, and Development delays including disability, covering 30+ conditions and surgeries at District Early Intervention Centres.
how_to_apply: Screening is conducted directly in schools and Anganwadis by Mobile Health Teams. Parents are referred to District Early Intervention Centres (DEICs) if conditions are identified.
documents_required: School/Anganwadi identity or registration; Birth certificate / MCP card
summary_en: A programme that screens children from birth to 18 years for health problems such as birth defects, deficiencies, diseases and developmental delays, and arranges early treatment. Teams visit anganwadi centres and schools.

title: Poshan Abhiyaan
objective: National mission to reduce malnutrition in children, adolescents and mothers.
eligibility: Pregnant women, lactating mothers, adolescent girls, and children aged 0 to 6 years across all districts.
benefits: Multi-ministerial convergence to reduce stunting, wasting, underweight, and anemia through technology-led monitoring (Poshan Tracker app), fortified supplementary nutrition, and community awareness drives.
how_to_apply: Enroll at the local Anganwadi Centre (AWC) under the Women and Child Development department.
documents_required: Aadhaar of mother/child; MCP card; Basic family details
summary_en: Poshan Abhiyaan is the national mission against malnutrition. It works to improve the nutrition of young children, adolescent girls, pregnant women and nursing mothers through anganwadi centres, community campaigns and monitoring.

title: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana
objective: Nutrition support payments for tuberculosis patients during treatment.
eligibility: All notified tuberculosis (TB) patients diagnosed and undergoing treatment under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP).
benefits: Direct benefit transfer (DBT) of Rs 1,000 per month (or Rs 500/month as revised) to every notified TB patient throughout the duration of anti-TB treatment to meet nutritional needs.
how_to_apply: Notification by treating doctor/clinic into the Ni-kshay digital portal (tbcindia.gov.in). The local TB health visitor (TBHV) assists with bank details verification.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Bank passbook/account details; TB diagnosis and treatment card
summary_en: This scheme gives nutrition support payments to people being treated for tuberculosis so they can eat better during treatment. Payments are made to the patient's bank account. TB patients usually get this through the local health facility.

title: Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana
objective: Builds tertiary healthcare capacity, including new AIIMS-like institutes.
eligibility: Public healthcare infrastructure program benefiting the general public across underserved states; not an individual beneficiary enrollment scheme.
benefits: Correction of regional imbalances in quality tertiary healthcare by setting up 22 new All India Institutes of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) and upgrading state government medical colleges.
how_to_apply: No individual application required. Avail outpatient, inpatient, and emergency super-specialty treatment directly at AIIMS and upgraded government medical colleges.
documents_required: Standard hospital OPD registration ID proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID)
summary_en: A scheme that strengthens advanced hospital care in India, including setting up new AIIMS-type institutes and upgrading medical colleges. Citizens do not apply; they benefit by using the hospitals and institutes it builds.

title: Samagra Shiksha
objective: Combined programme for school education from pre-school to class 12.
eligibility: Students from pre-school through Class 12 enrolled in government and government-aided schools across all states and union territories.
benefits: Free textbooks, school uniforms, transport allowance, ICT labs, vocational education, and infrastructure grants to schools to ensure equitable and inclusive quality school education.
how_to_apply: Enroll directly in any government or local authority school. School administration implements benefits under state education departments.
documents_required: Birth certificate / Aadhaar; Transfer certificate (if changing schools); Passport photos
summary_en: Samagra Shiksha is the Centre's main programme for school education, from pre-school to class 12. It supports schools, teachers, textbooks, digital learning and inclusive education, and works through state education departments.

title: PM POSHAN (Mid-Day Meal Scheme)
objective: Hot cooked meals in schools to improve nutrition and attendance.
eligibility: Children in Classes 1 to 8 studying in government, government-aided schools, special training centres, and madrasas supported under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan.
benefits: Free hot cooked nutritious meal every school day providing 450 calories and 12g protein for primary classes, and 700 calories and 20g protein for upper primary classes.
how_to_apply: Provided automatically to every enrolled student attending school on academic working days. No separate application needed.
documents_required: School enrollment record
summary_en: This scheme provides a hot cooked meal to children in eligible schools on school days. It is meant to improve nutrition and increase school attendance. The meal is arranged by the school, so families do not apply separately.

title: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao
objective: Campaign to protect girl children and promote their education.
eligibility: Girl children and women across all Indian districts, with focus on districts having low Child Sex Ratio (CSR).
benefits: Awareness campaigns against gender-biased sex selection, multi-sectoral support for girl child education, retention in schools, and sanitary facilities.
how_to_apply: Community advocacy and educational incentive scheme implemented through district collectors and Anganwadis; no single individual application.
documents_required: None for community schemes; School enrollment documents for educational interventions
summary_en: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is a campaign to protect girl children and support their education. It works through awareness drives and coordination between the women and child development, health and education departments.

title: National Scholarship Portal
objective: Single online portal for applying to central and state scholarships.
eligibility: Students from Pre-Matric to Post-Doctoral levels belonging to SC, ST, OBC, minority communities, EWS, or disabled categories meeting scheme-specific merit and parental income limits.
benefits: Single window digital gateway disbursing pre-matric, post-matric, merit-cum-means, and top-class scholarships directly into students' bank accounts via DBT.
how_to_apply: Register and submit online scholarship application at scholarships.gov.in using Aadhaar authentication and upload institutional verification certificates.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Bank passbook linked to Aadhaar; Previous year academic marksheet; Family income certificate; Caste/Community certificate
summary_en: The National Scholarship Portal is one online site where students can find and apply for scholarships offered by central and state governments and other bodies. Students register, fill one application and choose the scholarships they qualify for.

title: PM Vidyalaxmi
objective: Collateral-free education loans for meritorious students at top institutions.
eligibility: Students admitted into top-ranked higher education institutions (NIRF ranked) who require financial assistance for tuition and college expenses.
benefits: Collateral-free, guarantor-free education loans covering full tuition and academic fees, with 75% credit guarantee and interest subventions up to 3% for students with parental income up to Rs 8 lakh.
how_to_apply: Register on the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal (pmvidyalaxmi.gov.in) and apply with Common Education Loan Application Form (CELAF) for participating banks.
documents_required: Aadhaar; PAN; Admission letter from eligible institution; Fee structure document; Class 10/12/degree marksheet; Income certificate
summary_en: PM Vidyalaxmi helps meritorious students get education loans for admission to top-ranked higher education institutions. The loans are designed to be collateral-free and guarantor-free for eligible students. Students apply through a single online portal.

title: PM SHRI Schools
objective: Model schools that showcase the National Education Policy.
eligibility: Students enrolled in selected exemplary schools managed by Central/State/UT governments and local bodies.
benefits: Modern green school infrastructure, smart classrooms, science labs, experiential learning pedagogies, and ICT curriculum aligned with NEP 2020.
how_to_apply: Admissions through standard state/central school admission procedures (e.g., Kendriya Vidyalaya, Navodaya, or state government schools selected as PM SHRI).
documents_required: Birth certificate; Previous academic records; Aadhaar; Category certificate (if applicable)
summary_en: PM SHRI schools are model schools chosen from existing government schools, built to show how the National Education Policy 2020 can work in practice. They aim for modern teaching, better facilities and inclusive learning. Parents do not apply separately.

title: SWAYAM
objective: Free online courses from school level to postgraduate level.
eligibility: Anyone from school students (Class 9-12) to undergraduate, postgraduate, working professionals, and lifelong learners.
benefits: Free access to thousands of high-quality digital university-level courses designed by premier faculty (IITs, IIMs, IISc, NCERT), with credit transfer recognized by UGC/AICTE upon passing proctored exam.
how_to_apply: Sign up for free at swayam.gov.in using Google, Microsoft, or email account, and enroll in any scheduled course.
documents_required: None for learning; Identity proof (Aadhaar/College ID) required only when registering for proctored certificate examination
summary_en: SWAYAM is a free online platform that offers courses from school level up to postgraduate level. Learners can study at their own pace and, for many courses, take an exam to get a certificate. Registration is free.

title: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme
objective: Supports employers who train apprentices, with a share of the stipend.
eligibility: Candidates aged 14 years and above (18+ for hazardous occupations) holding 5th/8th/10th/12th/ITI/diploma/degree qualifications.
benefits: Government shares 25% of the prescribed monthly stipend (up to Rs 1,500 per month per apprentice) paid by employers, promoting on-the-job industrial apprenticeship training.
how_to_apply: Register as an apprentice on the national apprenticeship portal (apprenticeshipindia.gov.in) and apply to listed employer vacancies.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Educational qualification marksheets/certificates; Bank passbook; Passport size photo
summary_en: This scheme encourages employers to train apprentices by sharing part of the stipend cost. Young people can find apprenticeship opportunities and register on the apprenticeship portal, and gain skills with a stipend.

title: Right to Education Act 2009
objective: Law guaranteeing free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14.
eligibility: Every child between the ages of 6 and 14 years residing in India. Also mandates 25% reservation in private schools for children from Economically Weaker Sections (EWS).
benefits: Free and compulsory elementary education (Classes 1 to 8) without any tuition fee, capitation fee, or screening procedure.
how_to_apply: Enroll at any government or local school. For 25% private school quota under Section 12(1)(c), apply via state RTE online portals during annual lottery windows.
documents_required: Birth certificate or Anganwadi record; Residence proof; Income certificate and Caste certificate (for 25% private quota admissions)
summary_en: The Right to Education Act is a law that gives children aged 6 to 14 the right to free and compulsory elementary education. Private schools must reserve a share of seats for children from weaker sections. Admission is handled through the school and local education office.

title: Khelo India
objective: Programme to build sports culture and find young talent.
eligibility: Talented young athletes identified across schools and district sports tournaments (age groups U-14, U-17, U-21).
benefits: Financial assistance of Rs 5 lakh per annum for 8 years to identified talented athletes, high-performance coaching, world-class sports academy infrastructure, and national sports competitions.
how_to_apply: Register on the Khelo India athlete portal (kheloindia.gov.in) and participate in district/state talent identification trials and Khelo India Youth/University Games.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Date of birth certificate; Sports achievements/merit certificates; Medical fitness certificate; Bank passbook
summary_en: Khelo India is a national programme to build a strong sports culture and spot young talent. It supports sports infrastructure, talent identification and financial help for promising athletes, and organises games for young people.

title: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana
objective: Short-term skill training and certification for youth.
eligibility: Indian youth (aged 15-45) who are school/college dropouts or unemployed seeking industry-relevant skill training.
benefits: 100% government-funded short-term skill training, recognition of prior learning (RPL), certification, assessment fees, and placement assistance with financial reward upon passing.
how_to_apply: Register online at skillindia.gov.in or pmkvyofficial.org, or visit any accredited Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendra (PMKK).
documents_required: Aadhaar card; Bank account details; Educational qualification documents; Passport size photographs
summary_en: This scheme offers short-term skill training and certification for young people, so that they can find work or start their own work. Training is given through approved training centres in many job roles.

title: Skill India Mission
objective: National mission to train people in job skills at scale.
eligibility: Indian youth, job seekers, and unorganized workers looking to acquire technical and vocational skills across diverse industrial trades.
benefits: Umbrella national framework delivering industry-aligned vocational qualifications (NSQF), technical certifications, apprenticeships, and international mobility pathways.
how_to_apply: Explore courses and training partners on skillindiadigital.gov.in and enroll at affiliated training centres (PMKK/ITIs).
documents_required: Aadhaar; Proof of education; Bank details; Photos
summary_en: Skill India Mission is the national effort to train people in job skills at scale. It brings together skill training, apprenticeships and certification, and provides one place to find courses and training providers.

title: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
objective: Guarantees up to 100 days of paid manual work per year to rural households that ask for it.
eligibility: Any adult member of a rural household who is willing to do unskilled manual work.
benefits: Legal guarantee of at least 100 days of wage employment in every financial year. Guaranteed minimum wage paid directly to bank/post office account within 15 days, with statutory unemployment allowance if work is not provided within 15 days of demand.
how_to_apply: Submit an oral or written application to the local Gram Panchayat to receive a free MGNREGA Job Card, then submit a demand for work.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Proof of residence in village; Bank or post office savings account details; Passport photos
summary_en: This law guarantees up to 100 days of paid unskilled manual work a year to rural households that ask for it. Work includes building roads, ponds and other local assets. Households apply for a job card at the Gram Panchayat.

title: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
objective: Builds women's self-help groups and rural livelihoods.
eligibility: Rural poor households, especially women belonging to SC/ST, single women, landless laborers, and disabled persons, organized into Self Help Groups (SHGs).
benefits: Revolving fund (Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000 per SHG), Community Investment Fund (CIF), collateral-free bank loans up to Rs 20 lakh with interest subvention down to 7%, and livelihood skill training.
how_to_apply: Join an existing village Self Help Group (SHG) or form a new 10-20 member women's SHG with the help of Community Resource Persons (CRPs) or Gram Panchayat coordinators.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Bank account passbook; Ration card; SHG membership resolution
summary_en: This mission helps rural women, especially from poor households, form self-help groups and improve their incomes. It supports savings, credit, training and links to markets. Women join through local groups and community organisations.

title: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Urban Livelihoods Mission
objective: Skills, credit and shelter support for the urban poor.
eligibility: Urban poor, street vendors, slum dwellers, homeless individuals, and urban unemployed youth.
benefits: Skill training with placement, interest subsidy on bank loans for setting up micro-enterprises (up to Rs 2 lakh for individuals and Rs 10 lakh for groups), development of vendor markets, and permanent 24/7 urban shelters.
how_to_apply: Apply through your Urban Local Body (Municipality/Municipal Corporation) or Community Organizer under the City Mission Management Unit.
documents_required: Aadhaar; BPL proof / urban poor certificate; Bank account details; Project proposal for enterprise loan
summary_en: This mission helps the urban poor through skill training, support for self-employment, shelters for the homeless and support for street vendors. It is run through urban local bodies.

title: PM Street Vendor's AatmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi)
objective: Affordable working-capital loans for street vendors.
eligibility: Urban street vendors vending on or before March 24, 2020 (and later extended dates) possessing Certificate of Vending / ID card issued by ULB or letter of recommendation.
benefits: Collateral-free working capital loan starting at Rs 10,000 (1st tranche), Rs 20,000 upon timely repayment (2nd tranche), and Rs 50,000 (3rd tranche) with 7% per annum interest subsidy and monthly cashbacks on digital transactions up to Rs 1,200/year.
how_to_apply: Apply online via the PM SVANidhi portal (pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in) or PM SVANidhi mobile app, or through Common Service Centres (CSCs).
documents_required: Aadhaar; Certificate of Vending (CoV) / Urban Local Body ID / Letter of Recommendation; Bank passbook; Mobile number linked to Aadhaar
summary_en: PM SVANidhi gives street vendors affordable working-capital loans so they can restart or grow their business. Vendors who repay on time can become eligible for larger loans, and digital payments are encouraged.

title: PM Vishwakarma
department: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises
objective: Recognition, training, tools and credit for traditional artisans and craftspeople.
eligibility: Traditional artisans and craftspeople working with their hands and tools in 18 specified trades (carpenter, blacksmith, goldsmith, potter, sculptor, cobbler, tailor, etc.) aged 18+, with one beneficiary per family.
benefits: PM Vishwakarma Certificate & ID card, 5-7 days basic skill training with Rs 500/day stipend, Rs 15,000 toolkit e-voucher, collateral-free credit up to Rs 1 lakh (first tranche) and Rs 2 lakh (second tranche) at concessional 5% interest rate, and digital transaction incentives.
how_to_apply: Apply through nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with biometric verification on pmvishwakarma.gov.in.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Mobile number linked to Aadhaar; Bank account details; Ration card (mandatory for family verification); Trade details
summary_en: PM Vishwakarma supports traditional artisans and craftspeople. It offers recognition with an ID card, skills training, toolkit support and affordable credit. Applications are made through the official portal or Common Service Centres.

title: Stand-Up India
objective: Bank loans for first-time entrepreneurs from SC/ST groups and women.
eligibility: SC, ST, and/or woman entrepreneurs aged 18 and above setting up a greenfield enterprise in manufacturing, services, agri-allied activities, or trading.
benefits: Bank loans between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore covering up to 85% of project cost with low margin money requirement and handholding support through SIDBI.
how_to_apply: Apply online via standupmitra.in or directly at any scheduled commercial bank branch.
documents_required: Aadhaar; PAN; Caste certificate (for SC/ST); Business project report; Proof of business address; Bank statement (6 months)
summary_en: Stand-Up India helps people from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women who want to start a new enterprise. It encourages banks to give loans for setting up a first business in manufacturing, services or trading.

title: Startup India
objective: Recognition and support for new startups.
eligibility: Entities incorporated as Private Limited, LLP, or Registered Partnership in India within 10 years, with annual turnover under Rs 100 crore and focused on innovation/scalability.
benefits: DPIIT recognition offering 3-year income tax exemption under 80-IAC, exemption from Angel Tax (Section 56), 80% rebate in patent filing fees, self-certification under 9 labor/environmental laws, and access to Fund of Funds.
how_to_apply: Register online at startupindia.gov.in and apply for DPIIT recognition with incorporation details and pitch deck.
documents_required: Certificate of Incorporation / Registration; PAN; Pitch deck / brief description of innovative nature of business; Website / app link
summary_en: Startup India is a government initiative to support new startups. It offers recognition for eligible startups and helps with information, mentoring and access to funding and certain benefits. Founders apply for recognition on the official portal.

title: Make in India
objective: Initiative to encourage manufacturing and investment in India.
eligibility: Domestic and global companies, manufacturers, investors, and industrial enterprises operating across 27 designated champion sectors.
benefits: FDI liberalization up to 100% in most sectors, streamlined clearances via National Single Window System (NSWS), capital subsidies under Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, and industrial corridor infrastructure.
how_to_apply: Investors can explore investment opportunities, project clearances, and single-window statutory approvals at makeinindia.com and nsws.gov.in.
documents_required: Company incorporation documents; Industrial project profile; Financial and investment statements; Regulatory registrations
summary_en: Make in India encourages companies to manufacture in India and invest here. It focuses on easing business rules, attracting investment and building manufacturing across many sectors. It is mainly relevant to businesses and investors.

title: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
department: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises
objective: Credit-linked subsidy for setting up new micro enterprises.
eligibility: Any individual above 18 years of age (minimum 8th pass for projects above Rs 10 lakh in manufacturing or Rs 5 lakh in services). SHGs and cooperative societies are also eligible.
benefits: Credit-linked capital subsidy on bank-financed micro-enterprises: up to Rs 50 lakh for manufacturing and Rs 20 lakh for services, with margin money subsidy of 15% to 35% based on location (rural/urban) and social category.
how_to_apply: Submit an online application on the KVIC portal (kviconline.gov.in/pmegpeportal) selecting the implementing agency (KVIC, KVIB, or DIC).
documents_required: Aadhaar; PAN; Educational qualification certificate (8th class marksheet or higher); Detailed Project Report (DPR); Caste/Special category certificate; Rural area certificate (if applicable)
summary_en: PMEGP is a scheme that helps people set up new small enterprises by giving a subsidy linked to a bank loan. Applicants usually apply online and the loan comes from a bank.

title: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
department: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises
objective: Guarantee cover that lets banks lend to small businesses without collateral.
eligibility: New and existing Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) in manufacturing and services sector seeking credit from Member Lending Institutions (MLIs).
benefits: Collateral-free credit facility up to Rs 5 crore per borrower, with credit guarantee coverage between 75% and 85% provided by CGTMSE to lending banks.
how_to_apply: Approach any scheduled commercial bank, selected RRBs, or NBFCs participating in CGTMSE and request a collateral-free loan under the CGTMSE guarantee scheme.
documents_required: Business registration / Udyam Certificate; Detailed Project Report (DPR); PAN; Financial statements/ITR; Bank statements
summary_en: This trust gives banks a guarantee cover so they can lend to micro and small enterprises without asking for collateral or a third-party guarantee on eligible loans. Businesses apply for the loan from their bank or lender.

title: Udyam Registration
department: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises
objective: Free online registration for micro, small and medium enterprises.
eligibility: Any business entity qualifying as Micro (investment <= Rs 1 cr, turnover <= Rs 5 cr), Small (<= Rs 10 cr / <= Rs 50 cr), or Medium (<= Rs 50 cr / <= Rs 250 cr).
benefits: Official MSME registration certificate with permanent dynamic QR code. Unlocks priority sector lending, lower bank interest rates, protection against delayed payments (MSMED Act), subsidies on patents and ISO certifications, and concessions on electricity.
how_to_apply: Complete 100% free paperless registration at udyamregistration.gov.in using Aadhaar and PAN.
documents_required: Aadhaar number of proprietor/partner/director; PAN card of enterprise/proprietor; GSTIN (if applicable); Bank account details
summary_en: Udyam Registration is the free online registration for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Registered businesses get a certificate that helps them use MSME benefits such as easier credit. Registration is done on the official portal.

title: e-Shram
objective: National database and ID for unorganised workers.
eligibility: Unorganized workers aged 16 to 59 years, not an income-tax payer and not a member of EPFO or ESIC (e.g., gig workers, construction workers, domestic helpers, rickshaw pullers, street vendors).
benefits: 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN) e-Shram card that centralizes social security benefits, accidental death/permanent disability cover of Rs 2 lakh (Rs 1 lakh for partial disability), and national database integration for disaster relief.
how_to_apply: Self-register for free on eshram.gov.in using Aadhaar OTP, or visit the nearest CSC or state seva kendra.
documents_required: Aadhaar number; Mobile number linked to Aadhaar; Savings bank account number and IFSC code
summary_en: e-Shram is a national database of unorganised workers. Workers can register and get a unique ID that helps them access social security schemes. Registration is free and can be done online or at Common Service Centres.

title: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan
objective: Pension scheme for unorganised workers.
eligibility: Unorganized workers aged 18 to 40 years with monthly income of Rs 15,000 or less, not covered under EPFO, ESIC, or NPS, and not paying income tax.
benefits: Assured minimum monthly pension of Rs 3,000 upon reaching age 60. Beneficiary contributes Rs 55 to Rs 200 monthly with 50% matching contribution from Central Government. 50% family pension for spouse upon death.
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) or self-enroll at maandhan.in with auto-debit bank mandate.
documents_required: Aadhaar card; Savings bank account passbook / Jan Dhan account with IFSC code; Mobile number
summary_en: This is a pension scheme for unorganised workers such as domestic workers, street vendors and drivers. Workers who join make a small monthly contribution and receive a pension after reaching the required age. Check the official site for the age limits and amounts.

title: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana
objective: Basic bank accounts for every household.
eligibility: Any Indian citizen aged 10 years or older who does not have an existing basic bank account.
benefits: Zero-balance Basic Savings Bank Deposit (BSBD) account, free RuPay debit card with Rs 2 lakh accidental insurance coverage, overdraft facility up to Rs 10,000 for eligible accounts, and seamless DBT connectivity.
how_to_apply: Visit any bank branch, Bank Mitra kiosk, or customer service point (CSP) and fill the PMJDY account opening form.
documents_required: Aadhaar card (or any Officially Valid Document: Voter ID, Driving License, Passport, NREGA job card); Passport size photograph
summary_en: The Jan Dhan Yojana is the national drive to give every household a bank account. Accounts are opened with simple requirements and can receive direct benefit transfers, along with other basic banking facilities. Account holders can open one at any bank branch.

title: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
objective: Low-cost life insurance for bank account holders.
eligibility: Individuals aged 18 to 50 years holding an active bank or post office savings account who give consent for auto-debit.
benefits: Life insurance coverage of Rs 2 lakh payable to the nominee upon death of the insured due to any cause, for a low annual premium of Rs 436.
how_to_apply: Apply through net banking, mobile banking app, or submit an auto-debit consent form at your bank/post office branch.
documents_required: Aadhaar (for e-KYC); Savings bank account passbook; Nominee details
summary_en: This is a low-cost life insurance scheme for bank account holders. Those who enrol pay a small yearly premium and the family receives a payout if the insured person dies during the cover period. Enrolment is done at your bank.

title: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana
objective: Low-cost accident insurance for bank account holders.
eligibility: Individuals aged 18 to 70 years having a savings bank or post office account with auto-debit authorization.
benefits: Accidental insurance cover of Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or permanent total disability, and Rs 1 lakh for permanent partial disability, for an annual premium of just Rs 20.
how_to_apply: Enable through your bank's net banking portal / mobile app, or visit your branch and sign the auto-debit authorization form.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Savings bank account details; Nominee identification details
summary_en: This is a low-cost accident insurance scheme for bank account holders. Those who enrol pay a small yearly premium and get a payout in case of accidental death or disability. Enrolment is done at your bank or through net banking.

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
objective: Small savings account for the future education and marriage needs of a girl child.
eligibility: Parents or legal guardians of a girl child from her birth until she turns 10 years of age (maximum two girl children per family, three in case of twins/triplets).
benefits: High sovereign-guaranteed interest rate (currently 8.2% p.a.), Section 80C tax deduction up to Rs 1.5 lakh, tax-free interest and maturity (EEE status), partial withdrawal for higher education at age 18, and full maturity after 21 years.
how_to_apply: Open an account at any post office or authorized public/private commercial bank branch by filling the SSY account opening form.
documents_required: Girl child's birth certificate; Identity proof and address proof of parent/guardian (Aadhaar/PAN); Passport photos of parent/guardian
summary_en: A government savings scheme for the girl child. Parents or guardians can open an account in a girl's name at a post office or authorised bank, and save for her future education and marriage. Interest rates are set by the government and change from time to time.

title: National Pension System
objective: Voluntary long-term retirement savings scheme.
eligibility: Any Indian citizen (resident or non-resident) aged between 18 and 70 years.
benefits: Low-cost voluntary market-linked retirement savings scheme managed by PFRDA. Offers compound growth, additional tax deduction up to Rs 50,000 under Section 80CCD(1B), and at age 60 provides 60% tax-free lump sum withdrawal with 40% converted into a lifelong monthly annuity.
how_to_apply: Open a PRAN account online at enps.nsdl.com or via eNPS portals of points of presence (POPs), or visit registered POP-SP bank branches.
documents_required: Aadhaar or PAN for KYC; Cancelled cheque or bank passbook; Scanned copy of signature and photograph
summary_en: The National Pension System is a voluntary long-term retirement savings scheme. People contribute regularly during their working life and receive a pension after retirement. It is regulated by PFRDA, and accounts can be opened through banks or online.

title: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme
objective: Post office and bank savings scheme for people aged 60 and above.
eligibility: Individuals aged 60 years or above, or retired individuals aged 55-60 who took voluntary retirement (VRS), and retired defense personnel aged 50+.
benefits: Government-backed regular quarterly income scheme offering attractive interest rate (currently 8.2% p.a.), maximum deposit limit of Rs 30 lakh, 5-year tenure (extendable by 3 years), and tax deduction under Section 80C.
how_to_apply: Open an account by submitting Form A at any designated post office or commercial bank branch.
documents_required: Aadhaar; PAN card; Age proof; Retirement proof/pension payment order (for retirees aged 55-60); Two passport size photos
summary_en: A government savings scheme for people aged 60 and above. It offers regular interest income for senior citizens. It is available through post offices and authorised banks, and interest rates change from time to time.

title: Mahila Samman Savings Certificate
objective: One-time small savings option for women and girls, available for a limited period.
eligibility: Girls or women of any age (accounts for minors can be opened by a parent or legal guardian).
benefits: Fixed 2-year deposit scheme offering a guaranteed interest rate of 7.5% per annum compounded quarterly, maximum investment limit of Rs 2 lakh, and partial withdrawal facility up to 40% after one year.
how_to_apply: Submit an application form at any post office branch or authorized public/private sector bank.
documents_required: Aadhaar; PAN; Account opening form; KYC documents of applicant/guardian
summary_en: This small savings option was offered for a limited period for women and girls through post offices and certain banks. Check the official site to see whether it is still open.

title: National Social Assistance Programme
objective: Pensions for elderly, widows and persons with disabilities from poor households.
eligibility: Elderly (60+), widows (40-79), and persons with severe disabilities (18-79 with 80%+ disability) belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) households.
benefits: Monthly non-contributory social assistance pensions: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), Widow Pension (IGNWPS), Disability Pension (IGNDPS), and National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS lump sum of Rs 20,000 upon breadwinner's death).
how_to_apply: Apply through the Block Development Office (BDO), Gram Panchayat, or Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO) in rural areas, or Municipality in urban areas.
documents_required: Aadhaar; BPL ration card / SECC enumeration proof; Age proof; Disability certificate (for IGNDPS); Death certificate of husband (for IGNWPS); Bank passbook
summary_en: This programme provides social security pensions to elderly people, widows and persons with disabilities from poor households. It is run with state governments, who handle applications through local offices.

title: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana
department: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
objective: Free foodgrains for eligible ration card holders.
eligibility: All Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households and Priority Household (PHH) ration cardholders covered under the National Food Security Act.
benefits: Completely free foodgrains (5 kg of rice/wheat per person per month for PHH families, and 35 kg per family per month for AAY households) delivered via Fair Price Shops.
how_to_apply: No separate application needed. Existing NFSA ration cardholders collect rations directly from their local Fair Price Shop (FPS) via biometric e-PoS authentication.
documents_required: Valid NFSA Ration Card; Aadhaar of family members linked to ration card
summary_en: This scheme provides free foodgrains to eligible ration card holders. It is handled through the public distribution system and fair price shops. Check the official site for the current status and quantity.

title: National Food Security Act 2013
department: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
objective: Legal right to subsidised foodgrains for eligible households.
eligibility: Up to 75% of rural population and 50% of urban population identified by states as Priority Households (PHH) and Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) families.
benefits: Legal entitlement to subsidized foodgrains (5 kg per person per month at Rs 3/kg rice, Rs 2/kg wheat, Rs 1/kg coarse grains, currently provided free under PMGKAY), along with nutritional support to pregnant women and children.
how_to_apply: Apply for a ration card through your state Food and Civil Supplies Department portal or local Tehsil / Food Supply Office.
documents_required: Aadhaar of all family members; Proof of residence; Income certificate / BPL proof; Family group photograph
summary_en: The National Food Security Act gives eligible households a legal right to subsidised foodgrains, and provides special nutrition support for pregnant women, nursing mothers and children. It is delivered through ration cards and fair price shops.

title: One Nation One Ration Card
department: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
objective: Lets ration card holders collect their entitlement from any fair price shop in the country.
eligibility: All NFSA ration cardholders, particularly migrant workers and laborers who relocate across states for work.
benefits: Nationwide portability of food security entitlements. Beneficiaries can lift their subsidized or free foodgrains from any Fair Price Shop across India using their existing ration card and biometric e-PoS authentication.
how_to_apply: No new registration required. Ensure your existing ration card is linked with Aadhaar for all family members.
documents_required: Ration card number; Aadhaar number; Biometric fingerprint/iris authentication at FPS
summary_en: One Nation One Ration Card lets ration card holders collect their entitlement from any fair price shop in the country. It is especially useful for migrant workers and families who move for work. Beneficiaries are verified at the shop.

title: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin
objective: Financial help for rural families without a pucca house to build one.
eligibility: Rural families living in kutcha/dilapidated houses or houseless households identified via SECC 2011 and Awaas+ survey, who do not own a pucca house.
benefits: Financial assistance of Rs 1.20 lakh in plains and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly/difficult/northeast states for constructing a 25 sq.m. pucca house, plus 90-95 days of unskilled labor wages under MGNREGA and Rs 12,000 for toilet construction under SBM-G.
how_to_apply: Beneficiary list is verified by the Gram Sabha from the Awaas+ list; Gram Panchayat officials facilitate registration and geo-tagging on the AwaasSoft portal.
documents_required: Aadhaar card; Bank account passbook; Job Card number (MGNREGA); Land ownership document; Swachh Bharat toilet registration ID
summary_en: PMAY-Gramin helps rural families without a pucca house to build one. Eligible families receive financial help for construction. Beneficiaries are identified through official lists, so check with your Gram Panchayat.

title: Swachh Bharat Mission
objective: National campaign for sanitation, toilets and clean communities.
eligibility: Rural and urban households without individual household latrines (IHHL), communities requiring public toilets, and urban local bodies.
benefits: Financial incentive of Rs 12,000 for constructing an Individual Household Latrine (IHHL), community sanitary complexes, solid and liquid waste management infrastructure, and open-defecation-free sustainability.
how_to_apply: Apply online at sbm.gov.in (rural) or swachhbharaturban.gov.in (urban), or submit through the Gram Panchayat / ULB ward office.
documents_required: Aadhaar card; Bank account passbook; Electricity bill or residence proof; Photograph of applicant and construction site
summary_en: Swachh Bharat Mission is the national campaign for sanitation. It supports building toilets, safe waste disposal and clean communities, with separate programmes for rural and urban areas.

title: Jal Jeevan Mission
objective: Tap water connections for rural households.
eligibility: Every rural household, village school, Anganwadi centre, and community health centre across all states and union territories.
benefits: Provision of Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) providing safe and adequate drinking water at 55 liters per capita per day (lpcd) on a regular and long-term basis.
how_to_apply: Community-driven scheme executed through Village Water and Sanitation Committees (Pani Samitis). Tap connections are installed door-to-door without individual consumer fees.
documents_required: Aadhaar / Village household survey identification
summary_en: Jal Jeevan Mission aims to provide tap water connections to rural households. It is run with states and local communities, and focuses on safe and regular water supply. Villages plan and manage the water systems.

title: AMRUT
objective: Water supply, sewerage and green space projects in cities.
eligibility: Urban local bodies in 500 designated cities and towns across India; benefits all urban residents.
benefits: Universal coverage of water supply, sewerage networks, storm water drainage, urban green spaces, non-motorized transport, and municipal administrative reforms.
how_to_apply: Administered directly by Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities). Citizens connect to newly laid water/sewer networks through standard municipal utility service applications.
documents_required: Property ownership / Municipal property tax receipt; Aadhaar; Utility connection application form
summary_en: AMRUT supports basic services in cities, such as water supply, sewerage, stormwater drainage and green spaces. Citizens benefit through improvements delivered by their city governments.

title: Smart Cities Mission
objective: Develops selected cities with better infrastructure and technology.
eligibility: 100 selected cities across India undergoing urban renewal and area-based development.
benefits: Integrated Command and Control Centres (ICCC), smart mobility, intelligent traffic management, smart water and power grids, improved urban living standards, and citizen safety.
how_to_apply: Centrally sponsored city infrastructure initiative; citizens access benefits through integrated city services, portals, and citizen feedback portals.
documents_required: None for public infrastructure access
summary_en: The Smart Cities Mission develops selected cities with better infrastructure and technology. It funds projects such as improved public spaces, transport and digital services.

title: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
objective: All-weather road connectivity to rural habitations.
eligibility: Unconnected rural habitations with a population of 500+ persons in plains and 250+ in hilly, tribal, and desert areas.
benefits: All-weather blacktopped road connectivity linking unconnected rural habitations to major markets and highways, boosting rural economic growth and access to schools and hospitals.
how_to_apply: Habitations are identified through Comprehensive New Connectivity Priority Lists (CNCPL) executed by State Rural Roads Development Agencies (SRRDA).
documents_required: None for citizens (public infrastructure works)
summary_en: This scheme builds all-weather roads that connect rural habitations to markets, schools and health services. Roads are planned and built through state governments, so citizens do not apply for it.

title: Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana
objective: Rural electrification and separate power feeders for farm and household use.
eligibility: All un-electrified rural households and villages across India.
benefits: 100% village and rural household electrification, separation of agricultural and non-agricultural electricity feeders, and strengthening of rural sub-transmission and distribution networks.
how_to_apply: Households obtain electricity connections by applying to their local power distribution company (DISCOM) or village electrification camp.
documents_required: Aadhaar; Proof of residence; BPL card (for free connection under Saubhagya / DDUGJY guidelines)
summary_en: This scheme supports rural electrification and strengthens power supply in villages, including separating electricity lines for farms and households. It is run with state power companies.

title: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
objective: Subsidy for rooftop solar panels on homes to cut electricity bills.
eligibility: Indian households having a pucca roof suitable for solar panel installation and an active residential electricity connection with a DISCOM.
benefits: Direct financial capital subsidy up to Rs 30,000 for 1 kW, Rs 60,000 for 2 kW, and Rs 78,000 for systems of 3 kW or higher, providing up to 300 units of free monthly solar electricity and income from grid net-metering.
how_to_apply: Register on the national portal pmsuryaghar.gov.in, choose registered DISCOM and empanelled vendor, and apply for rooftop solar installation and net metering.
documents_required: Aadhaar card; Recent electricity bill; Electricity consumer account number; Bank account passbook/cancelled cheque
summary_en: This scheme encourages households to install rooftop solar panels by offering a subsidy. Households can reduce electricity bills and may be able to sell surplus power. Applications are made on the official portal.

title: SVAMITVA Scheme
objective: Property cards for rural homeowners, mapped using drones.
eligibility: Rural property owners residing in inhabited rural (Abadi) areas of villages across participating states.
benefits: Survey of rural land parcels using drone technology and issuance of official legal property cards ('Svamitva Property Cards') enabling rural citizens to use property as a financial asset for bank loans.
how_to_apply: Drone mapping is conducted village-wide by Survey of India and state Panchayati Raj departments. Property owners verify demarcations during ground ground-truthing camps.
documents_required: Aadhaar card; Existing village property ownership records / local revenue documents
summary_en: The SVAMITVA Scheme maps inhabited rural land using drones and gives property cards to rural homeowners. A property card helps people prove ownership of their house and use it for purposes such as loans.

title: Digital India
objective: Programme to make government services available digitally and improve connectivity.
eligibility: All citizens, businesses, government agencies, and educational institutions across India.
benefits: Universal digital infrastructure (BharatNet optical fiber), digital delivery of public services (UMANG, DigiLocker, UPI, e-Sign), and digital empowerment across society.
how_to_apply: Access government digital services through the UMANG unified mobile app (web.umang.gov.in) or respective government service portals.
documents_required: Aadhaar and mobile number for e-KYC authentication
summary_en: Digital India is the government's programme to make services available online and improve internet connectivity and digital skills. It covers many services, from identity to payments and online certificates.

title: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan
objective: Digital literacy training for rural households.
eligibility: Digitally illiterate individuals aged 14 to 60 years from rural households where no other family member is digitally literate.
benefits: Free 20-hour digital literacy training module teaching computer/smartphone operations, internet browsing, email, digital financial payments (UPI), and government online services.
how_to_apply: Enroll at the local Common Service Centre (CSC) or designated PMGDISHA training centre in the village.
documents_required: Aadhaar card; Mobile number; Self-declaration of digital illiteracy
summary_en: This programme gives digital literacy training to people in rural households, so they can use phones and computers for services such as payments and government schemes. Training is arranged through approved centres.

title: DigiLocker
objective: Secure online storage and sharing of official documents.
eligibility: Every Indian citizen possessing an Aadhaar number.
